turns.en: And compounding and compounding and compounding are you backed by institutional quality bond funds. Hi Longview listeners, we're taking a week off from new episodes.
turns.zh: 复利、复利、再复利，让你获得机构级品质的债券基金做后盾。《The Long View》的听众朋友们，我们这周停更一期。

turns.en: We hope you'll enjoy this conversation with our colleague Jeff Patak, which aired last month. We'll be back with a new episode next week. Thanks for listening.
turns.zh: 希望你们喜欢本期与我们同事 Jeff Ptak 的对话，这集是一个月前播出的。我们下周将带着新节目回归。感谢收听。

turns.en: Please stay tuned for important disclosure information at the conclusion of this episode. Hi, and welcome to the Longview. I'm Amy Arnott, Portfolio Strategist for Morningstar.
turns.zh: 请留在本集，重要披露信息将在结尾播出。大家好，欢迎收听《The Long View》，我是 Amy Arnott，Morningstar 的组合策略师（Portfolio Strategist）。

turns.en: And I'm Christine Benz, Director of Personal Finance and Retirement Planning for Morningstar. Our guest on the podcast today is Jeff Patak. He's a longtime Morningstar employee and currently serves as Managing Director for Morningstar Research Services.
turns.zh: 我是 Christine Benz，Morningstar 的个人理财与退休规划总监。今天节目的嘉宾是 Jeff Ptak，他是 Morningstar 的老员工，目前担任 Morningstar Research Services 的董事总经理。

turns.en: He originally joined Morningstar back in 2002 as a Senior Mutual Fund Analyst. Jeff was one of the original two co-hosts of this podcast and regularly posts his thoughts on Morningstar.com, Substack, X, and LinkedIn.
turns.zh: 他早在 2002 年就加入了 Morningstar，担任共同基金高级分析师。Jeff 也是这档播客最初的两位联合主持之一，经常在 Morningstar.com、Substack、X 和 LinkedIn 上分享他的想法。

turns.en: It's always great to catch up with Jeff because his research sifts through so much data to come up with really insightful takeaways. And one of the highlights from the podcast today was when he was talking about how such a small number of stocks tend to generate a disproportionate amount of the market returns and what that means for diversified, actively managed funds.
turns.zh: 能和 Jeff 交流总是很棒，因为他的研究能在海量数据里淘洗，总能提炼出真正有洞见的结论。今天这期节目的一个亮点，就是他谈到为数不多的股票往往贡献了不成比例的市场回报，以及这对主动管理型的分散化基金意味着什么。

turns.en: So we'll hear a bit more about that later in the podcast. Amy, I love the conversation too. And one of the things I appreciate most about Jeff's work is his focus on investor outcomes.
turns.zh: 稍后我们会听到更多关于这方面的内容。Amy，我也很喜欢这段对话，我最欣赏 Jeff 工作的一点，就是他对投资者实际结果（investor outcomes）的关注。

turns.en: So in the conversation, I loved the discussion of what target date funds get right for investors, as well as what a couple of them, what some of them may be missing.
turns.zh: 所以在这段对话里，我很喜欢关于目标日期基金（target date fund）做对了什么、以及一些目标日期基金可能欠缺了什么的讨论。

turns.en: So I thought that was a great part of the discussion as well. I agree. All right. Let's take a listen. Jeff, welcome to the Longview. Oh, thanks so much for having me.
turns.zh: 我觉得那部分讨论也很精彩。我们完全同意。好，那一起来听听吧。Jeff，欢迎来到《The Long View》。哦，非常感谢邀请我来。

turns.en: Well, it's always great to talk to you. So Jeff, you had up Morningstar's annual Mind the Gap research on investor returns, and the most recent edition is actually hot off the presses today as we're taping this episode.
turns.zh: 能和你聊天总是很开心。Jeff，你主导了 Morningstar 一年一度的 Mind the Gap 投资者回报研究，最新的这一版就在我们录制这集节目时刚刚新鲜出炉。

turns.en: What would you say is the biggest takeaway from this year's report? Sure thing. So we did put out the latest edition of Mind the Gap this morning as we speak.
turns.zh: 你觉得今年这份报告最大的收获是什么？好的，我们今早——就在我们说话的当下——发布了最新版 Mind the Gap。

turns.en: And I would say there's a few takeaways. Some of them are recurring. They're sort of familiar themes that we've sounded, but they're important nonetheless.
turns.zh: 我想有几个要点，其中一些是老生常谈，是我们一直在强调的熟悉主题，但依然很重要。

turns.en: The first is, I would say, simpler strategies tend to exhibit smaller gaps. That is, investors earned more of their funds total returns than did more complex strategies.
turns.zh: 第一，我会说，更简单的策略往往表现出更小的差距（gap）。也就是说，相比更复杂的策略，投资者在简单策略上获得了基金总回报中更大的那一部分。

turns.en: And we can give some examples of what's simple versus complex. Another theme that emerges is stand-alone options, things like multi-asset funds, target date funds.
turns.zh: 我们可以举些例子，说明什么算简单、什么算复杂。另一个浮现出来的主题是独立可用产品（stand-alone options），比如多资产基金、目标日期基金。

turns.en: Investors appear to have greater success using those than they did building blocks. And then lastly, and this is something that's shown itself quite vividly in previous studies and it's true of this year's, they struggle with more volatile funds.
turns.zh: 投资者用这些产品，似乎比用构建模块（building block）更成功。最后一点，这一点在以往研究中就已显现得淋漓尽致，今年同样如此——他们在波动性更大的基金上会很吃力。

turns.en: They push their buttons and we see wider gaps between investors' dollar-weighted returns and total returns in more volatile funds than we do in less volatile funds.
turns.zh: 波动基金容易拨动他们的心弦，我们会看到，在波动性较大的基金里，投资者的美元加权回报（dollar-weighted return）与总回报之间的差距，要比波动性较小的基金更大。

turns.en: In terms of what trips people up, I would say the single biggest thing is probably extrapolating. They'll see a fund perform in a particular way and they'll project that into the future and in the process they might rung foot themselves because perhaps performance will mean revert up or down.
turns.zh: 说到什么会把人绊倒，我会说最大的单一因素大概是外推（extrapolation）。他们看到某只基金以某种方式表现，就把这种表现投射到未来，在这个过程中可能会搬起石头砸自己的脚——因为业绩很可能会向上或向下均值回归。

turns.en: And that's the sort of thing that can give rise to gaps between once-dollar-weighted returns and the funds total returns. So Jeff, can you expound on that simple versus more complex point and also I'd love to hear your take on what is going on with the all-in-one funds that they do tend to result in better investor outcomes, that investors tend to stay the course a bit better in them?
turns.zh: 而这正是会导致投资者美元加权回报与基金总回报之间出现差距的原因。Jeff，你能详细讲讲简单与复杂这一点吗？我也很想听你的看法，那些一体化基金（all-in-one fund）到底发生了什么，为什么它们往往能带来更好的投资者结果，让投资者更能坚持持有？

turns.en: For sure. And so I would say probably the quintessential example of a simple fund is something like a target date fund. It's designed for stand-alone use.
turns.zh: 没问题。我想，简单基金最典型的例子大概就是目标日期基金。它的设计初衷就是独立使用。

turns.en: It covers all the major asset classes. They mechanize, rebalancing and adjust the asset mix over time and so it obviates the need for the investor to take action.
turns.zh: 它覆盖了所有主要资产类别，它会机械化地进行再平衡并随时间调整资产配置，从而免去了投资者自己动手的必要。

turns.en: They don't have to fiddle with it in any way. Contrast that with something like sort of a building block. It could even be a U.S. equity fund but maybe sort of an even better example would be something narrow like a sector equity fund or an alternatives fund and that's the sort of thing where you're having to make sort of an ad hoc discretionary decision to put it into your portfolio and then you have to maintain it over time.
turns.zh: 他们完全不需要去折腾。与之形成对比的是像构建模块那样的东西，它甚至可能是一只美国股票基金，但更好的例子，也许是像行业股票基金或另类投资（alternatives）基金这样狭窄的品种——这就需要你做出一次临时的、相机抉择（discretionary）的决定把它放进组合，然后还得长期维护它。

turns.en: And so I think that's a pretty stark difference. You've got one that is sort of truly no maintenance and then another one that requires you to take actions of various sort.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这是个相当鲜明的对比。一个是真正无需维护的，另一个则要求你采取各种行动。

turns.en: The more we have found investors do, the more they transact, the more they struggle to capture their funds total returns. And so I think that that plays a pretty significant role in explaining the difference between the amount of success that investors have had and more simple types of investments versus more complex type of investments.
turns.zh: 我们发现，投资者做得越多、交易得越多，就越难捕获到基金的总回报。所以我认为，这一点在相当大的程度上解释了投资者在简单类投资与复杂类投资上取得成功程度之间的差异。

turns.en: The other thing that I would quickly point to and that we can only infer this. We don't measure it in the study but it does seem that context, setting, circumstance are important to the type of results that investors realize.
turns.zh: 还有一点我想快速指出来——这个我们只能推断，研究里并没有直接度量——但情境、场所、环境看起来确实对投资者实现的结果类型很重要。

turns.en: A retirement plan is a kind of gilded cage. It's a more controlled purpose built environment. It's not really built for ad hoc discretionary.
turns.zh: 退休计划就像一个金笼（gilded cage），它是一个更受控、专门打造的环境，并不是为临时的相机抉择交易而设计的。

turns.en: Transacting contrast that with a self-directed brokerage account or even other types of of rapid IRA, what have you, where the investor has to kind of go in and maybe it allows for more frequent transacting, I think you see that express itself in some of the results that we see where some of these standalone options, which are typically found in the context of a retirement plan, do considerably better than other things that are less often
turns.zh: 与之形成对比的是自主管理的经纪账户，或者其他类型的 IRA 等等——投资者得自己进去操作，也许那里允许更频繁的交易。我认为这一点在我们看到的一些结果里有所体现，那些独立可用的选择，通常出现在退休计划的情境里，表现明显好于较少出现在退休计划里的其他品种。

turns.en: found in retirement plans. So having the type of freedom and flexibility that people kind of take for granted today with intraday trading for ETFs and no cost brokerage platforms is not necessarily a good thing in every way.
turns.zh: 所以，那种今天大家习以为常的自由和灵活——盘中交易 ETF、零成本经纪平台——未必在所有方面都是好事。

turns.en: You're right, you are. Yeah, so it's free quote unquote to trade and I'm sure that's very liberating for a certain segment of investors, but I think that one doesn't want to lose sight of other types of costs you can incur, including timing related effects, buying high, selling low as it were. And so I think it's something that we all need to keep in mind.
turns.zh: 你说得对，确实如此。是的，所谓「自由」地交易，对某一部分投资者来说肯定很令人振奋，但我想我们不能忽视其他类型的成本，包括与择时相关的效应——所谓的高买低卖。所以我觉得这是我们所有人都需要铭记的一点。

turns.en: So you mentioned more complex funds like sector funds and alternatives. Are there any specific categories that have had particularly wide gaps?
turns.zh: 那么，你提到了更复杂的基金，比如行业基金和另类投资。有没有哪些具体类别的差距特别大？

turns.en: You know, so we do look at particular Morningstar categories in the study, but we look at the 10 largest categories by assets. And what we found in this year's installment of the study is that pretty much across the board, you know, with the exception, I think of maybe some of the international stock categories, you saw pretty narrow gaps amongst those largest categories.
turns.zh: 你知道，我们确实在研究中考察具体的 Morningstar 类别，但我们看的是按资产规模排的前十个最大类别。在今年的这份研究里我们发现，基本上——我想除了某些国际股票类别之外——在这些最大类别中你看到的差距都相当窄。

turns.en: We didn't drill down and look at particular sort of specialized categories like a given sector equity category, given alts category. What we can observe at the overall category group level, so sector equity alternatives, is that we have tended to see wider gaps in absolute terms there.
turns.zh: 我们没有下钻去看那些专门的类别，比如某个行业股票类别、某个另类投资类别。我们能在总的类别组层面观察到——也就是行业股票、另类投资这些层面——那里的绝对差距我们历来看得更大。

turns.en: And again, I mean, they're more specialized. They tend to be used. It stands to reason in a more ad hoc discretionary way. And so it creates the sort of environment where, you know, investors are going to have to make choices about when to add, when to subtract, when to prune as it were.
turns.zh: 而且重申一次，它们更专门，按常理也会被以更临时的、相机抉择的方式使用。这就营造了一种环境：投资者不得不就何时加仓、何时减仓、何时修剪做出选择。

turns.en: And so that can cause some troubles, just given the fact that there's lots of stimuli and, you know, they might not make the optimal choices at those various times.
turns.zh: 所以这可能带来一些麻烦——光是考虑到外部刺激那么多，他们未必在各个时点都做出最优选择。

turns.en: And again, these are not typically found in the context of a retirement plan, which is a more controlled setting. And so I think it creates an environment that's even more conducive to over-transacting.
turns.zh: 而且这些品种通常不出现在退休计划这种更受控的情境里。所以我认为它营造的环境更有利于过度交易。

turns.en: So you did add a section in this year's report looking specifically at cryptocurrency funds, which have become much more widely available to average retail investors with the advent of spot Bitcoin ETFs and spot Ether ETFs.
turns.zh: 所以，你在今年的报告里增加了一个专门研究加密货币基金的部分。随着现货比特币 ETF（Spot Bitcoin ETF）和现货以太坊 ETF（Spot Ether ETF）的出现，这类产品已经大大更容易被普通散户投资者接触到。

turns.en: What were some of your findings there? Yeah, so we looked at it from the time the first batch of spot Bitcoin ETFs launched. This is January 2024.
turns.zh: 你在那部分有什么发现？是的，我们从第一批现货比特币 ETF 上市之时开始考察，那是 2024 年 1 月。

turns.en: We looked at it through June of 2026. And we found that based on our estimates, the average dollar invested in those crypto ETFs had lost money while the ETFs themselves, they earned a positive aggregate total return.
turns.zh: 我们一直考察到 2026 年 6 月。我们发现，根据我们的估算，投入到这些加密 ETF 里的平均每美元其实是在亏钱的，而 ETF 本身则获得了正的总回报。

turns.en: And so there was a very wide gap. And again, the dollar-weighted return was negative. And so I would say it's early days. And, you know, it could so happen that investors stay the course and crypto rallies.
turns.zh: 所以差距非常大。重申一次，美元加权回报是负的。所以我想说现在还是早期，也完全有可能投资者坚持持有、加密货币随后上涨。

turns.en: And then that gap will close and dollar-weighted returns, one hopes will improve. They'll be positive rather than negative as they were as of June 30, 2026.
turns.zh: 那样的话差距就会缩小，美元加权回报——人们会希望——会改善，由负转正，而不是像截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日那样是负的。

turns.en: You know, but it's an early worrisome sign that money sort of flooded in after we had seen a burst from Bitcoin. This was around the time they launched and soon after, only to see it roll over.
turns.zh: 你知道，这是一个令人担忧的早期信号：在我们看到比特币的一波上涨之后，资金蜂拥而入——那大概是在它们上市前后不久——然后却看到它回落。

turns.en: And that explains why they have the poor dollar-weighted results. So it's going to be important to see them stay the course. And then one hopes the cryptocurrency itself rallies and that burnishes their dollar-weighted results.
turns.zh: 这就解释了为什么它们的美元加权结果那么差。所以关键在于看他们能否坚持持有，然后人们会希望加密货币本身上涨，从而美化他们的美元加权结果。

turns.en: And if I remember correctly, the gap that you found for the crypto-related ETFs was something like 14 percentage points, which is an enormous gap and I think probably bigger than any other category that you might have looked at.
turns.zh: 如果我没记错的话，你为加密相关 ETF 发现的差距大概是 14 个百分点——这是一个巨大的差距，我想可能比你考察过的其他任何类别都要大。

turns.en: It's very wide. Yeah, that we went narrower on crypto than we did in a lot of other areas of the study where we tend to keep it at a higher level.
turns.zh: 非常宽。是的，我们在加密这块下钻得比研究里很多其他领域更细，那些领域我们往往停留在更高的层面。

turns.en: But you're right that it stood out as a very, very wide gap. So in terms of how to improve these statistics, if you were designing an investment platform entirely around minimizing some of these behavioral mistakes, some of these timing mistakes, what features would you build into it and what common industry practices would you eliminate?
turns.zh: 但你说的对，它确实作为一个非常非常宽的差距凸显了出来。那么，就如何改善这些统计数字而言，如果你要完全围绕减少这些行为失误、这些择时失误来设计一个投资平台，你会给它内置哪些功能，又会砍掉哪些常见的行业做法？

turns.en: So I would say mechanize, mechanize, mechanize. It wouldn't look that different than the way we auto-enroll DC participants into 401ks and then have them put their assets into a target date fund, assuming it's chosen as the default option, which it so often is.
turns.zh: 所以我会说，机械化、机械化、再机械化。它看起来不会和我们把确定缴费（Defined Contribution）计划的参与者自动注册（auto-enroll）进 401(k)、然后把他们的资产放进目标日期基金——假设它被选为默认选项，而它往往如此——的方式有多大不同。

turns.en: That's a very simple and automated workflow. It reduces frictions. In terms of deletions, things that I would rather go away, very narrow strategies, thematics in particular.
turns.zh: 那是一个非常简单、自动化的流程，它减少了摩擦。至于要删掉的东西——那些我希望消失的——就是很狭窄的策略，尤其是主题类基金（thematic fund）。

turns.en: We've done some work on that previously and found that the dollar-weighted returns in those things are just putrid and we can talk about what might give rise to those poor results.
turns.zh: 我们之前对这类东西做过一些研究，发现它们的美元加权回报糟糕透顶，我们可以聊聊是什么导致了这些糟糕的结果。

turns.en: But those are the sorts of strategies that I think really give investors trouble. And I think probably outcomes would be in a better place, albeit thematics are still not the dominant investing form.
turns.zh: 但这类策略是我觉得真正会给投资者带来麻烦的东西。我想，即使主题类基金目前还不是主流的投资形式，但如果它们更少一些，结果本来可能会更好。

turns.en: But I think that outcomes would be even better if there were fewer of them. So you've also written several articles about active management, including a piece called Have We Been Too Hard on Active Funds?
turns.zh: 不过我觉得，如果这类产品更少，结果会更好。你也写过好几篇关于主动管理的文章，其中一篇叫《Have We Been Too Hard on Active Funds?》（我们对主动基金太苛刻了吗？）。

turns.en: And you found that active managers deserve more credit than they often get. So what are some of your key findings there? What do you think are some of the limitations with research that has been done about that topic?
turns.zh: 你发现主动管理人的价值往往被低估了。那么，你在那里的主要发现是什么？你觉得关于这个主题已经做过的研究有哪些局限？

turns.en: Yep. So in that particular article, I was riffing on some academic work that had been done and these academics were looking at, it's a report called SPIVA.
turns.zh: 好的，在那篇具体文章里，我借鉴了一些已有的学术研究，那些学者研究了一份叫 SPIVA 的报告。

turns.en: It's put out by S&P and basically sort of a lead tables for active funds. They'll go and tally up the number of active funds that have succeeded versus their costless benchmarks over some interval of time.
turns.zh: SPIVA 由 S&P 发布，基本上算是主动基金的成绩排行榜。他们会去统计在一定时间段内，有多少主动基金跑赢了它们免成本的基准。

turns.en: So it could be like one, three, five, 10, 15, even 20 years if I'm not mistaken, if memory serves. And you know, these academics, and they did very thoughtful work, they focused on the methodology of that study.
turns.zh: 这个时间段可以是 1 年、3 年、5 年、10 年、15 年，甚至 20 年——如果我没记错、如果记忆可靠的话。而这些学者做了非常缜密的工作，他们聚焦在那项研究的方法论上。

turns.en: You know, and their conclusion was that SPIVA was painting sort of an unduly bleak picture of active funds success in beating their benchmark.
turns.zh: 你知道，他们的结论是，SPIVA 描绘了一幅主动基金跑赢基准情况被过分悲观的图景。

turns.en: I would say the most persuasive part of their paper was they said in lieu of costless indexes, you should use something like an asset weighted average of comparable passive funds.
turns.zh: 我认为他们论文里最有说服力的部分是，他们说，与其用免成本的指数，你应该用类似可比被动基金的资产加权平均。

turns.en: And I could definitely get behind that. It didn't change the results. That meaningfully, there were a couple of other methodological adjustments that they suggested.
turns.zh: 这一点我完全认同。那并没有实质性改变结果。他们还建议了几个其他方法论上的调整。

turns.en: But my overall takeaway was it didn't change the picture that drastically. I mean, I think even after they applied these changes, still like two thirds of active funds in aggregate were lagging their benchmarks, the ones that they had chosen this asset weighted average of passives.
turns.zh: 但我总体的体会是，它并没有让图景发生那么大变化。我的意思是，我觉得即便他们应用了这些改动，总体上仍有大约三分之二的主动基金跑输了它们所设定的基准——也就是那个被动基金资产加权平均。

turns.en: And, you know, that's still not an especially encouraging result. And that's notwithstanding some other sort of, I guess, quibbles I had with methodological choices that they made in their paper.
turns.zh: 你知道，那仍然算不上一个特别令人鼓舞的结果。且不说我对他们论文里做的一些方法论选择还有一些别的、我姑且称之为吹毛求疵的地方。

turns.en: So for me, it was it was a very, very interesting paper in a lot of ways, but I didn't find it very persuasive. You had another article called the biggest active stock funds picked the right stocks.
turns.zh: 所以对我来说，那是一篇在很多方面都非常非常有趣的论文，但我不觉得它很有说服力。你还写过另一篇文章，叫《The Biggest Active Stock Funds Picked the Right Stocks. They Still Lagged》（最大的主动股票基金选对了股票，却依然落后）。

turns.en: They still lagged in it. You suggest that stock selection wasn't necessarily the core problem with these lagging active funds. Does this imply that portfolio construction and implementation are now more important differentiators than security selection?
turns.zh: 你在文中提出，选股未必是这些落后主动基金的核心问题。这是否意味着，组合构建和执行如今已经比个券选择更重要的差异化因素？

turns.en: I think it does. That was one of my main takeaways from conducting this study. And, you know, to kind of boil down what I had done as part of this paper, I aggregated these managers stock holdings into a single pool.
turns.zh: 我觉得是的。这是我做这项研究的主要体会之一。要把我在这篇论文里所做的事情浓缩一下，我把这些经理的持股汇总成一个单一的投资池。

turns.en: And then I just let it go. I assumed that there were no changes made and then compare the results of that do nothing portfolio to these funds, actual aggregate results.
turns.zh: 然后我就放任不管，假设没有任何改动，再把这只「什么都不做」组合的结果，与这些基金实际汇总起来的结果做对比。

turns.en: And I found that, you know, in the most recent year I'd studied in the prior years and in the full 10 year period, this do nothing version did a heck of a lot better than the actual funds did.
turns.zh: 我发现，无论是我研究的最近一年、之前几年，还是完整的 10 年周期，这个「什么都不做」的版本都比这些基金实际表现好了很多很多。

turns.en: And that's, you know, it's a credit to the stock picking prowess of the managers of these very large funds. But it also, I think, points to an issue which you hit on, which is that they probably are doing they're not letting their winners run long enough and they're selling their winners off too early.
turns.zh: 这既是对这些超大型基金管理人选股功力的肯定，但我觉得，它也指向一个你恰好提到的问题，那就是他们很可能没有让赢家跑够久，而是过早地卖掉了他们的赢家。

turns.en: And so I think it probably reinforces that the next frontier in portfolio analysis and manager analysis is focusing on some of the portfolio construction and trading decisions that they have made along the way.
turns.zh: 所以我想，这大概印证了组合分析和经理分析的下一个前沿，是聚焦于他们沿途做出的某些组合构建和交易决策。

turns.en: It doesn't look like the missing and greeting. And it's the stock picking necessarily rather it looks like some of the choices that they make in maintaining the portfolio over time warrant further scrutiny.
turns.zh: 问题看起来不在于选股，也不在于择时，而更像是他们在长期维护组合过程中做出的某些选择，值得进一步审视。

turns.en: Yeah. So Christine and I interviewed Will Danoff at the conference a month or two ago and one of the big keys to his success has been letting his winners run exactly as you said.
turns.zh: 是的。Christine 和我一两个月前在会议上采访了 Will Danoff，他成功的一个大关键，正是你说的让赢家充分奔跑。嗯嗯，是的。

turns.en: Mm hmm. Yep. You've also written about research from Hendrik Besenbinder and other academics finding that a relatively small number of stocks have driven a disproportionate portion of recent market returns.
turns.zh: 你也写过关于 Hendrik Bessembinder 和其他学者的研究，他们发现相对较少的一小部分股票驱动了近些年来市场回报中不成比例的一大块。

turns.en: Does that sort of create a structural disadvantage for diversified active funds that have to manage things like liquidity and risk controls and limitations on their position sizes?
turns.zh: 这是否会给分散化的主动基金造成一种结构性劣势——这些基金不得不管理流动性、风险控制和对持仓规模的限制？

turns.en: I think it could create a disadvantage. It's not hopeless. And we still see plenty of active fund managers put up good numbers. You know, Besenbinder he's done awesome work.
turns.zh: 我觉得它可能会造成一种劣势。但也并非毫无希望，我们仍然看到很多主动基金经理交出了漂亮的成绩。Bessembinder 做了很棒的工作。

turns.en: And I actually would recommend listeners go back and listen to an interview that we did with him a little while back. You know, in the article I was being a little facetious, you know, in suggesting that maybe the structure the fund structure itself conspires against managers success.
turns.zh: 我其实会建议听众回头去听我们不久前和他做的那次访谈。在那篇文章里，我有点开玩笑地说，也许基金结构本身在暗中妨碍经理的成功。

turns.en: You know, but it's hard to overlook the fact that, you know, this tremendous skewness of returns that Besenbinder's research has found, you know, it is somewhat incompatible with the funds structure.
turns.zh: 但很难忽视这样一个事实，也就是 Bessembinder 研究所发现的这种回报的巨大偏度（skewness），它和基金结构多少有些不兼容。

turns.en: You know, because it stands to reason that you would you'd need to rely on sort of like power laws of the sort that you see more commonly in things like venture capital or a handful of mega winners kind of carry the portfolio.
turns.zh: 因为按常理，你需要依靠那种你在风险投资（venture capital）里更常见到的幂律（power law），也就是靠少数几个超级赢家来扛起整个组合。

turns.en: You know, but when that happens, you have all the associated concentration risk and volatility and scrutiny and, you know, not only can that bump up against some of the sort of operational regulatory realities, but then there are also the questions that you get, you know, from investors, you know, maybe it's been inculcated that you don't let positions get that big.
turns.zh: 可当那件事发生时，你就承担了所有相关的集中度风险、波动、审视——这不仅会撞上某些运营和监管现实，而且投资者也会提出种种质疑——也许大家已经根深蒂固地认为，不该让某个持仓变得那么大，不该去招致那么高的波动。

turns.en: You don't court that amount of volatility. So I think, you know, there's I think there's a bit of attention there. And I think it's one of the reasons why it's been particularly challenging for US stock fund managers over the past few decades.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，那里确实有些值得关注的地方，这也是过去几十年对美国股票基金经理来说尤其艰难的原因之一。

turns.en: Looking forward, what market environment would provide the strongest test of whether active management can truly add value after fees. We always hear from active managers that it's like, oh, wait, don't look at me during a bull market. I'll earn my keep in a weak market environment.
turns.zh: 展望未来，什么样的市场环境能最有力地检验主动管理是否真能在扣费后创造附加值？我们总能听到主动经理说，哦，别在牛市里看我，我会在疲软的市场环境里挣到我的佣金。

turns.en: What should be the sort of market climate that would show active managers or, you know, would sort of demonstrate whether they can add value for sure.
turns.zh: 什么样的市场气候才能真正检验出主动经理的水平，或者说，能证明他们究竟能否创造附加值？

turns.en: So I think truly is the operative term there. And so, you know, I think that if we were sort of putting sort of our academic hat on, we would say for it truly to be sort of compelling robust, it would have to be over a pretty long period of time.
turns.zh: 我觉得「真正」是这里的关键词。所以，如果我们戴上学术的眼镜，我们会说，要真正令人信服、稳健，就得经过相当长的一段时间。

turns.en: And, you know, that's going to outlast most investors, patients, the truth of that is, you know, but just in more sort of practical terms, I guess there are a couple of environments where I would expect active to do better and improve their model. The first is down markets. I think that this does get overplayed by active fund houses in particular, you know, that they do this, you know, heroic job of protecting the downside.
turns.zh: 而那段时间往往会超过大多数投资者的耐心——事实就是如此。但就更具实操意义而言，我想有这么两种环境我会预期主动表现更好、改善他们的处境。第一种是下跌市。我觉得这一点确实被主动基金公司特别夸大了，他们好像在为下行保护做了英雄般的表现。

turns.en: There is truth that they do better against their benchmarks largely for reasons of style and purity in down markets, you know, and we've done plenty of research on this that shows that, you know, so that's one environment where I would expect them to earn their keep.
turns.zh: 但确实存在这样的真相：它们在下跌市中跑赢基准，很大程度上是因为风格和持仓的纯粹性，我们就这一点做过大量研究，也证明了这一点。所以那是一个我会预期他们能挣到佣金的环境。

turns.en: Another is when we see, you know, big stylistic dislocations, you know, probably the quintessential example of that would be a time like 2000, where you saw this big break between growth and value and large and small and domestic and foreign and right. So there were all of these different dislocations. And that can create real opportunities for a manager. And so we can't predict when that will happen. But when it happens, it's the sort of environment that should set up a little bit better for active funds.
turns.zh: 另一种是我们看到巨大的风格错位（stylistic dislocation）的时候，最典型的例子大概就是 2000 年那样的时期，你看到成长与价值、大盘与小盘、国内与国外之间出现了巨大断裂。这些种种错位，能为经理创造真正的机会。我们无法预测它何时发生，但一旦发生，那是应该对主动基金稍微有利一点的环境。

turns.en: And one would hope they would do better. So those are sort of two examples of where I would be looking for them to earn their keep. Jeff, I wanted to ask about active fixed income. When I've looked at the data does appear that active fixed income looks a little better than certainly active large cap equity. Are there spots where investors, you know, might reasonably select a low cost active fund and as fixed income perhaps one?
turns.zh: 所以人们会希望他们那时表现得更好。那就是我会看他们能否挣到佣金的两个例子。Jeff，我想问问固定收益的主动管理。我看数据的时候，主动固定收益似乎确实比主动大盘股要好一些。有没有哪些领域，投资者可以合理地选择一只低成本的主动基金，也许在固定收益里就有一个？

turns.en: I think so. Yeah, I think you're you're on the money. When you look at the results for active fixed income and our colleagues I think have written some pieces to this effect. They are meaningfully better than what you would see and certainly in domestic equity, even foreign equity.
turns.zh: 我想是的。你说得正中要害。当你看主动固定收益的结果时——我想我们的同事写过一些这方面的文章——它们明显好于你在国内股票、甚至海外股票里所看到的。

turns.en: So I think that you can make a better case that we can sort of talk about some of the technical factors that might explain why active can be more efficacious in that realm than us. I guess probably on the scope of the conversation. But it's an example of where I think to be circumspect.
turns.zh: 所以我认为你可以做出一个更好的论证——我们可以谈谈那些可能解释主动在固定收益领域比在美股更有效的技术性因素，但那大概超出了我们对话的范围。但这是一个我认为要审慎对待的例子。

turns.en: In fact, you want to give it a good hard look. I'm a very ardent believer in minimizing fees, but also I recognize that there are instances where it can make sense to maybe pay up a little bit. And that can be an example for you can make a case for it.
turns.zh: 事实上，你应该好好审视一番。我是一个非常坚定的费率最小化信奉者，但我也承认，确实存在一些情形，也许多付一点钱是合理的——这就是一个你可以为之论证的例子。

turns.en: We've also seen some other sort of niche areas where it looks like it can make more sense to, you know, to use active if you're really determined to get exposure to it, like one that springs to mind is like foreign small cap, right?
turns.zh: 我们还看到一些其他的细分领域，在那里看起来用主动更合理一些——如果你确实很想获得某种敞口的话。比如一个马上想到的就是海外小盘股，对吧？

turns.en: You know, there are sort of like ETFs and indexes that are out there, you know, but that's that's sort of a capacity constrained, you know, somewhat esoteric area to begin with. And so that's the sort of place where, you know, maybe you would consider active, but you're going to pay for it.
turns.zh: 你知道，外面也有 ETF 和指数，但那是产能受限（capacity-constrained）、多少有些深奥的领域。所以那正是你可能会考虑主动的地方，但你得为此付费。

turns.en: Those are not cheap strategies. And so I think you would want to have the highest conviction before you made that decision. So in thinking about my own journey as an investor, when I first started out in my early 20s, I had a very small portfolio, but it was pretty much all active with actively managed funds. And over time, the portfolio has gotten a little bit bigger and is much more tilted toward the passive side.
turns.zh: 那些都不是便宜的策略。所以我想，在做那个决定之前，你希望自己的信心达到最高。说到我自己作为投资者的旅程，我刚开始、二十岁出头的时候，我的投资组合很小，但几乎全是主动管理的基金。随着时间推移，组合变大了些，也更多地倒向了被动那一侧。

turns.en: And I'm curious if you have also shifted more toward passive vehicles in your own portfolio over time. Yeah, that's true of me as well, Amy. And so and it sounds like my journey has, has resembled yours. You know, I, I came into the firm back 2002, I was covering active funds, I was certainly investing in our 401k plan, which was populated with index and active funds alike.
turns.zh: 我也很好奇，随着时间推移，你自己在组合里是不是也更多地转向了被动工具。是的，对我来说也是如此，Amy。听起来我的旅程和你的很像。我 2002 年进公司时负责覆盖主动基金，我当时肯定也在我们的 401(k) 计划里投了钱，那里面既有指数基金也有主动基金。

turns.en: And, you know, I really was very enthused about investing with active fund managers. And so those are still a part of my portfolio. But as time has worn on, it shifted increasingly towards passive and that I can speak for other immediate family members who have their own investment portfolios and maybe rubbed off on them a bit, but they are invested exclusively in index funds. And, and so it's, you know, I think that it's probably born of experience.
turns.zh: 我当时对用主动基金经理投资真的非常热心。所以它们至今仍是我组合的一部分。但随着时间推移，它越来越多地转向了被动。我可以说我其他直系家人也各自有投资组合，也许我把这点传染给了他们一点，但他们只投指数基金。所以我想，这大概是源于经验。

turns.en: You can't necessarily know in some cases that, you know, passive is the better choice in some of these circumstances. And so maybe you've had to go with active fund managers and, you know, saw some of the limitations there.
turns.zh: 在某些情况下，你未必能知道被动在这些情形里是更好的选择，所以也许你不得不跟着主动基金经理走，然后看到了他们的一些局限。

turns.en: Fortunately, we've got a great set of active funds that are on our 401k plan menu. And so I'm pleased, you know, to invest with those managers and continue to do so into the future. But yeah, I've, you know, I've gotten the fever for passive as well as time has gone on.
turns.zh: 幸运的是，我们 401(k) 计划菜单上有一组很棒的主动基金，所以我很乐意继续和这些经理一起投资，未来也会如此。但是的，随着时间推移，我也染上了被动的热情。

turns.en: And tax implications, I think, figure into all of our thinking. 100%. Yep. Yeah. Yeah. So we wanted to shift gears. You recently testified before Congress and we'll try to drop a link to that into the show notes. But you testified that investor success depends heavily on lower costs and greater transparency.
turns.zh: 我想税务影响也融入了我们每个人的考量。百分之百。是的，是的。所以，我们想换个话题。你最近在国会作证了，我们会试着把链接放到节目注记里。你作证时说，投资者的成功在很大程度上依赖于更低的成本和更大的透明度。

turns.en: So if regulators could implement only one reform to make things better for investors, what would have the greatest positive impact on long term investor outcomes?
turns.zh: 那么，如果监管机构只能推行一项改革来让投资者处境更好，哪一项对长期投资者结果的最大正面影响？

turns.en: Yeah, it's a great question. It wasn't part of my testimony. And as a practical matter, it was, it was a little bit peripheral to the hearings focus.
turns.zh: 这是个很好的问题，它并不在我的证词里。就实操而言，它与听证会的焦点有点外围。

turns.en: I think the thing that would have the greatest aggregate impact on long term incomes is, is wider access to high quality, low cost retirement plans. I know we, we pride ourselves on, you know, our system of, I don't know if you want to call it rugged individualism, you know, it no doubt has benefited many in our society.
turns.zh: 我认为对长期收入有最大总体影响的事情，是让更多人有机会获得高品质、低成本的退休计划。我知道我们为自己的体系感到自豪——我不知道该不该叫它 rugged individualism，它无疑让社会上很多人受益。

turns.en: But, you know, we also know that there are many who don't have access to a retirement plan at all. And so, you know, just trying to think big picture, you know, bringing them into the fold would have, I think, a huge positive impact.
turns.zh: 但我们也知道，有很多人根本没有退休计划可用。所以，从宏观大局想想，把他们纳入这个体系，我想会有巨大的正面影响。

turns.en: And our other message, you know, that we tried to convey through our testimony is, overall, this, the story that we've seen play out in the fund industry for investors is encouraging. It's affirming, you know, costs have come down.
turns.zh: 我们想通过证词传达的另一个信息是：总体而言，我们在基金行业为投资者看到的这个故事是令人鼓舞的、是肯定的——成本已经下降。

turns.en: Investors have increasingly, you know, been embracing diversification and vehicles that deliver that passive funds in particular. And we think that's, you know, redounded to their success. I mean, it's really helped them.
turns.zh: 投资者越来越多地拥抱了分散化，以及提供这种分散化的工具，尤其是被动基金。我们认为这有利于他们的成功，真的帮到了他们。

turns.en: But we wanted to encourage them to build on that, not to sort of backtrack or water down. I know there's there's one initiative in which, you know, companies will report less frequently.
turns.zh: 但我想鼓励他们在此基础上继续建设，不要往回退，也不要淡化。我知道有一项倡议，就是公司会减少报告的频率。

turns.en: And my own personal opinion is that as a step in the wrong direction, the opinions even within Morningstar vary on that. But that's the sort of thing where I would hope, you know, we would redouble our commitment to transparency, rather than take a step back as, as I think we have in that particular case.
turns.zh: 就我个人而言，我认为那是一个错误的步骤，即便在 Morningstar 内部，人们对这一点也意见不一。但那正是我希望我们会加倍致力于透明度、而不是后退一步的地方——我想在那种具体情形里我们正是后退了。

turns.en: So you've written a number of articles highlighting costs as one of the most reliable predictors of future success. Are there any cases in which investors might want to deliberately choose a higher cost strategy?
turns.zh: 你写过很多文章，强调成本是未来成功最可靠的预测因素之一。有没有哪些情形，投资者也许会想刻意选择一个成本更高的策略？

turns.en: Yeah, it's a great question. We talked about fixed income. Active fixed income might be one example. And then I think there are some other cases where, you know, you might argue that, you know, you don't want to make perfect the enemy of good.
turns.zh: 这是个很好的问题。我们谈到了固定收益，主动固定收益也许就是一个例子。然后我觉得还有一些其他情形，你可以争辩说——别让完美成了好的敌人。

turns.en: And probably the example that springs to mind, most readily to mind is, you know, where it's maybe it's a little bit more convenient for you, it removes some frictions, maybe it ensures that your dollar weighted outcomes are going to be better than perhaps they otherwise would be if you were investing in, say, a cheaper fund that's available to you in a particular way. And like to give an example, so think of like, I mean, it's a little niche, but like, you know, ETFs are funds that ladder bonds for you.
turns.zh: 最容易想到的例子，也许是那样一种情形：它对你来说可能更方便一点，减少了某些摩擦，也许能确保你的美元加权结果会比你若以某种特定方式投一只更便宜的基金要好。举个例子——虽然有点细分——像帮你把债券排成梯次（bond laddering）的 ETF。

turns.en: Like, I know I can hear the howls from some quarters that like, why would you pay a little bit more to do something as sort of simple and mundane as that? You know, simple and mundane can be monumental to some, you know, or there just could be frictions involved.
turns.zh: 我知道我都能听到某些人的抗议：你为什么要多付一点钱，去做一件这么简单、这么平凡的事呢？简单和平凡对某些人来说可能就是头等大事，或者那里就是涉及某些摩擦。

turns.en: And it can be worth it to do that sort of thing. Even more heretical in some quarters is a suggestion that, you know, maybe it can make sense in certain circumstances and stages of life to buy an annuity.
turns.zh: 所以值得那样做。在某些人看来更离经叛道的，是这样一种建议：也许在人生某些特定情形和阶段，买一份年金（annuity）是合理的。

turns.en: There are certainly, you know, tradeoffs that are involved in doing so. There's no question about it. But for some who need the permission to spend, it can be the right choice. And I know that you've had a number of guests on this podcast who have spoken about that dynamic.
turns.zh: 那里固然有涉及的取舍，这毫无疑问。但对于那些需要「允许自己花钱」的人来说，它可能是正确的选择。我知道你在这档播客上请过不少嘉宾谈过这种动态。

turns.en: And so it's another example where it can make sense. And even more heretical than that, I'll just give you sort of an example in the ETF space because I've been looking at these things.
turns.zh: 所以那是另一个它可能合理的例子。比那还要离经叛道一点，我就再给你一个 ETF 领域的例子，因为我一直在研究这些东西。

turns.en: Buffer ETFs, I would not recommend them for somebody that's an accumulation stage. They cost a lot. They cut off the tops of equity returns because they're built on options. That's how you get the downside protection.
turns.zh: 缓冲型 ETF（Buffer ETF），我不会推荐给处于积累阶段的人。它们成本很高，它们因为建立在期权之上会砍掉股票回报的上限——那是你获得下行保护的方式。

turns.en: However, I would say for a certain cohort of investors who are maybe approaching or at or even in retirement, they can make some sense. And we've actually seen encouraging dollar-weighted results with Buffer ETFs.
turns.zh: 不过，我会说，对于某一类也许临近退休、已经退休、甚至正在领取退休金的投资者，它们可能有点道理。我们实际上在缓冲型 ETF 上看到了令人鼓舞的美元加权结果。

turns.en: That was part of the Mind the Gap study that we put out today. I would say there can be a place for that type of structure for a certain type of investor that's in a certain place in their investing journey.
turns.zh: 那是我们今天发布的 Mind the Gap 研究的一部分。我会说，对于处于投资旅程某个特定位置的某类投资者，这种结构可以有一席之地。

turns.en: So there's just some kind of quick examples where you might want to think about paying up a little bit. So in general, we've seen a pretty benevolent trend where fees have come down in the fund industry. Investors have been selecting the low-cost funds.
turns.zh: 所以这只是一些快速举例，你可以考虑也许多付一点钱的地方。总体而言，我们看到了一个相当良善的趋势：基金行业的费用在下降，投资者一直在挑选低成本的基金。

turns.en: But advisor fees have been kind of stuck. Michael Kitzis has documented this. The 1% AUM fee is still the industry standard for investors with kind of average portfolio sizes.
turns.zh: 但顾问费用却一直卡在那里。Michael Kitces 记录了这一点。对于组合规模中等的投资者，1% 的资产管理费（AUM fee）仍然是行业标准。

turns.en: And of course, a well-qualified advisor can help investors get better outcomes. But how do you think investors should assess whether they're getting good value for money from their advisor?
turns.zh: 当然，一名合格的顾问能帮助投资者取得更好的结果。但你觉得投资者该如何评估自己从顾问那里得到的钱是否物有所值？

turns.en: I think if it's for supposed investing or asset allocation acumen alone, I'd be pretty skeptical. Very few professional investors beat their indexes by that margin before fees.
turns.zh: 我想，如果单纯是所谓的投资或资产配置眼光，我会相当怀疑。在收费之前，很少有专业投资者能凭那种优势跑赢指数。

turns.en: So I'm not sure why you'd expect your advisor to add at least that amount of value, especially if they're allocating to funds. Beyond that, I think it's going to depend on facts and circumstances, which I realize is a very wishy-washy answer.
turns.zh: 所以我不确定你为什么会指望你的顾问至少增加那么多价值，尤其是当他们只是在配置到各种基金的时候。除此之外，我想这得取决于具体事实和情形，我知道这是个很含糊的回答。

turns.en: But it's hard to say whether the advice you get will be worth at least 1% of your assets. I don't use an advisor, but I guess a question that I might ask myself is more the counterfactual.
turns.zh: 但很难说你得到的建议是否值得你资产的至少 1%。我自己不用顾问，但我想，我可能会问自己的一个问题更像是反事实——

turns.en: Will you be more than 1% worse off without the help you get? And sometimes that can be the more salient question for someone who knows they need advice, but they're not quite sure what sort of advice they need, let alone what's a fair fee to pay for it should be asking themselves. Do I think I'm in a position where there's real gaps in my knowledge or I'm just not sure how to navigate what can be a complex field,
turns.zh: 如果没有你得到的帮助，你会不会糟糕超过 1%？有时候，对那些知道自己需要建议、但不太确定需要哪种建议、更不知道为此付多少才合理的人来说，这才是更切题的问题。他们应该问自己：我是不是处在这样一种位置——我的知识存在实实在在的缺口，或者我只是不确定如何在可能相当复杂的领域里应对？

turns.en: especially if you're approaching retirement. If I don't engage an advisor, whether that's 1%, whether it's 2%, it's hard to say. So I think it's a valid model for certain relationships and circumstances.
turns.zh: 尤其当你临近退休时，如果不请一个顾问，无论是 1% 还是 2%，很难说会怎样。所以我觉得，对于某些关系和某些情形，那是一个站得住脚的模式。

turns.en: I think you also have done a great job on this podcast of bringing others who employ other models and provide terrific advice and planning to their clients. And it could be much more economical and easy to predict what it is you're going to outlay as the person receiving that advice.
turns.zh: 我想你也在这档播客上做得很好，把其他采用不同模式、为客户提供出色建议和规划的人请了进来。作为接受建议的那个人，你可能更经济、也更容易预测你要支出多少。

turns.en: So I think that's a very valid format model as well as opposed to the 1% fee. So sorry, it's short on specifics, but that's kind of the way I would try to approach it if I were somebody that's receiving advice.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得那也是一种很站得住脚的模式，相对于 1% 的费用。抱歉，它在细节上有点单薄，但如果我是那个接受建议的人，我会大致这样去看待它。

turns.en: As a financial advisor, you've got your clients back and we've got yours. With Vanguard's actively managed bond funds, you're backed by consistent performance with a low cost edge for an advantage that keeps compounding and compounding and compounding and sorry, quick break for legal. To learn more, visit vanguard.com slash audio. All investing is subject to risk. Investments and bonds are subject to interest rate credit and inflation risk Vanguard Marketing Corporation distributor.
turns.zh: 作为理财顾问，你有你的客户做后盾，我们有我们的客户做后盾。借助 Vanguard 的主动管理型债券基金，你将获得稳健业绩的支撑，加上低成本优势，让这一优势不断复利、复利、再复利……抱歉，先插播一段法律提示。想了解更多，请访问 vanguard.com/audio。所有投资都有风险，债券投资面临利率、信用和通胀风险，发行方为 Vanguard Marketing Corporation。

turns.en: And compounding, and compounding, and compounding. Are you backed by institutional quality bond funds? Vanguard. Oh, that's helpful. Thank you. We also wanted to touch on private markets and some of the product innovations that are going on there, which you also mentioned a minute ago.
turns.zh: 复利、复利、再复利，让你获得机构级品质的债券基金做后盾。Vanguard。哦，那很有帮助，谢谢。我们还想了想谈谈私募市场（private market）和那里正在发生的一些产品创新——你也在一分钟前提到了。

turns.en: And you've written extensively about some of the vehicles that have SpaceX related exposure and some of the challenges of packaging private assets into a vehicle that has daily liquidity.
turns.zh: 你也写过大量文章，探讨一些带有 SpaceX 敞口的载体，以及把私募资产（private assets）打包进一只具备每日流动性（daily liquidity）的工具中所面临的挑战。

turns.en: What are some of the key takeaways for investors from those examples? I would say it's a careful what you wish for situation. As we have this conversation, I think SpaceX maybe traded up a little bit this morning, but as of the close yesterday, that was trading meaningfully below the IPO price.
turns.zh: 从这些例子中，投资者能得到哪些关键要点？我会说，这是一种「小心你想要的东西」的局面。就在我们对话的同时，我想 SpaceX 今早可能涨了一点，但截至昨天收盘，它是在 IPO 价格下方明显交易的。

turns.en: And so as a result, some of the products that took a stake in it pre IPO were underwater on the position that's certainly not true of every one of those.
turns.zh: 因此，一些在 IPO 之前就建仓的产品，在那个头寸上目前是浮亏的，当然并非每一只都如此。

turns.en: You know, but I think for, you know, investors who are clamoring for exposure pre IPO, that probably seems like a pretty foreign situation that they now find themselves in given the sheer amount of hype.
turns.zh: 但对于那些在 IPO 之前就迫切想要获得敞口的投资者，考虑到那种铺天盖地的炒作，这大概是一种如今让他们觉得很陌生的处境。

turns.en: In your right, there is a fundamental incompatibility, in my opinion, between the daily liquidity structure. And so this is an ETF and open end fund, though I think it's more acute for ETFs and something that doesn't trade.
turns.zh: 你说得对，在我看来，每日流动性的结构——这是一只 ETF 和一只开放式基金——与一种不交易的资产之间存在根本的不兼容，而且我认为对 ETF 来说这种矛盾更尖锐。

turns.en: I mean, you know, ETFs are built for assets that, you know, one can readily value and transact in and that is not how you would describe a pre IPO name like SpaceX or anything else for that matter.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，ETF 是为那些可以轻易估值和交易的资产而打造的，而这绝不是你描述一只像 SpaceX 这样的 IPO 前股票——或者别的任何东西——时会用的方式。

turns.en: And so, you know, personally, you know, at the risk of selling like a scold or a worry war, it is a trend that concerns me just because I think you can basically have some real sort of complications that arise once you take a stake in one of these names in that type of wrapper.
turns.zh: 所以，就个人而言——冒着像个说教者或杞人忧天者的风险——这个趋势让我担忧，因为我觉得，一旦你在这样一只「包装」里持有这类股票的仓位，基本上就会引出一些实实在在的复杂问题。

turns.en: So I think I know what you're going to say, Jeff, but I'd like to hear your take on adding private market exposure as an investment option for 401k plans, either separately or as part of a diversified target date fund.
turns.zh: 所以我想我知道你接下来要说什么，Jeff，但我想听听你对把私募市场敞口作为 401(k) 计划投资选项的看法，无论是单独配置，还是作为分散化目标日期基金的一部分。

turns.en: It seems like private equity and credit are creeping closer to the retail channel. So I'd like to get your take on that broad question and then 401k specifically.
turns.zh: 看起来私募股权（private equity）和私募信用（private credit）正在一步步逼近零售渠道。所以我想先听你对这个大问题、然后专门就 401(k) 的看法。

turns.en: Where are you going to predict? I'd say I hate it because if so, you're, you're correct. I hate it. To me, it seems totally unnecessary to be fair.
turns.zh: 你会预测什么？我想说——如果真是那样，你说得对——我讨厌它。在我看来，坦率地说，这完全没有必要。

turns.en: You know, target date allocations have evolved over time. More has come into the fold. The retirement plan lineups have evolved. There are maybe more options that are available to investors.
turns.zh: 你知道，目标日期（target date）的配置随时间在演化，有更多东西被纳入了进来，退休计划的阵容也在演化，投资者可用的选项也许更多了。

turns.en: And so, you know, I could have taken that position 20 years ago and been like, oh, all you need is, you know, U.S. stocks and investment grade bonds and you're good to go.
turns.zh: 所以，我本可以在 20 年前就持那种立场，说哦，你只需要美国股票和投资级债券就够了，别的都不需要。

turns.en: We don't need this other stuff. But I just, I think there's a crucial difference here. You know, we're talking about liquid and illiquid. And, you know, you're also talking about, you know, a retirement plan. This is a linchpin part of our system and ensuring that, you know, when people reach their retirement years, they're able to enjoy them bountifully.
turns.zh: 但我觉得这里有一个关键区别。我们谈论的是流动与非流动。而且你也谈的是一个退休计划，这是我们体系的一个枢纽环节，它确保人们在进入退休年龄时能够丰裕地享受晚年。

turns.en: And I just, I do worry about introducing something that is illiquid in the context of a retirement plan. I think the least worst way to do it is through a target date fund.
turns.zh: 我只是担心在退休计划的情境里引入某种非流动的东西。我认为最不那么糟糕的做法，是通过目标日期基金来做。

turns.en: It does not seem advisable at all for it to be a standalone option on a menu. That seems like a recipe for disaster. So if they're going to do it, one would hope that they do it tucked away within a target date fund.
turns.zh: 让它成为菜单上一个独立的选项，看起来完全不可取，那似乎是通往灾难的配方。所以如果他们真要做，人们会希望它被藏在一只目标日期基金里。

turns.en: But in general, it just, it seems like, you know, a solution in search of a problem. I think by every indication I've seen, while there's plenty of work to do on our retirement system expanding access and the like, it seems like investors are faring pretty well.
turns.zh: 但总体而言，这看起来像是为一个不存在的问题寻找解决方案。就我所见到的种种迹象而言——尽管我们的退休体系在扩大覆盖面等方面还有大量工作要做——投资者过得还算不错。

turns.en: You know, they're doing well on target date funds. They're capturing their returns. We're getting them auto-enrolled. They're even auto-escalating.
turns.zh: 他们在目标日期基金上表现良好，他们在捕获自己的回报，我们让他们自动注册，甚至自动递增缴费（auto-escalate）。

turns.en: And so to me, that's a picture of success that we can build on. It doesn't seem like they've been deprived of anything, let alone private equity and credit. So I'm not a fan.
turns.zh: 所以在我看来，那是一幅我们可以建立于其上的成功图景。他们似乎并没有被剥夺任何东西，更不用说私募股权和私募信用了。所以我不支持。

turns.en: You've also written extensively about thematic portfolios and some of the risks involved in products like an AI-themed ETF. Why do you think investors are still so attracted to these types of thematic products, even though we have pretty strong evidence that investor results have been pretty poor?
turns.zh: 你也写过很多关于主题组合的文章，以及像一只 AI 主题 ETF 这类产品所涉及的风险。既然我们有相当强的证据表明投资者的结果相当糟糕，你为什么认为投资者仍然如此被这类主题产品吸引？

turns.en: It's a great question. You know, it's the power of stories. I think to a degree, people love stories. I think they find them especially compelling when maybe they confirm some of their priors.
turns.zh: 这是个很好的问题。这就是故事的力量。我想在某种程度上，人们热爱故事。我觉得，当故事也许印证了他们某些先入之见时，他们尤其会觉得它有说服力。

turns.en: You know, when it's intoxicating, when the story that maybe taps into their confirmation bias is being validated in the market at that time, there's some theme.
turns.zh: 当那个也许触及他们确认偏误（confirmation bias）的故事恰好在那个时点被市场验证、某个主题正当红时——就令人陶醉。

turns.en: And it squares with your intuition. You're like, yes, absolutely, this is going to be huge. And then furthermore, you see a vehicle that purports to tap into that theme is doing really, really well at the time.
turns.zh: 它和你的直觉相吻合，你会说：是的，绝对，这会火。再者，你看到一只声称能切入那个主题的载体在当时表现得非常好。

turns.en: I mean, you know, that's like ding, ding, ding. Those are three things that I think, you know, just really speak to a segment of investors. And I think it explains sort of the enduring power of thematic strategies, drawing assets, notwithstanding the results, which as I mentioned earlier, you know, I've found at a dollar-weighted basis have been really poor.
turns.zh: 那就像叮、叮、叮——我想这三件事真的说中了某一部分投资者。我认为这也解释了主题策略那种持久的吸金能力，尽管它们的结果，正如我之前所说，我在美元加权基础上发现相当糟糕。

turns.en: You've argued that investors should be cautious about products tied to the prediction markets. How do you distinguish between useful financial innovation and innovation that primarily serves speculative demand?
turns.zh: 你曾主张投资者应对与预测市场（prediction market）相关的产品保持谨慎。你如何区分有用的金融创新与主要服务于投机需求的创新？

turns.en: Yeah, so I think it comes down to its two things, time horizon and cash flows. The shorter the time horizon, like a single day, which is what sort of leverage ETFs and the like are built for, the more dubious the proposition.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得这归结为两点：时间跨度和现金流。时间跨度越短，比如像单日——这正是杠杆 ETF 之类所打造的——那这个命题就越可疑。

turns.en: I mean, that's pure speculation, because none of us know what's going to happen in a given day. If there are no cash flows associated with a security, then I think that veers towards speculation too.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，那是纯粹的投机，因为我们谁都不知道某一天会发生什么。如果一只证券不伴随着任何现金流，那我觉得它也滑向了投机。

turns.en: And I have to say, I'd lump crypto in with that, just given the fact that I haven't really seen somebody convincingly demonstrate its financial utility.
turns.zh: 我得说，我会把加密货币也归入其中，仅仅是因为我还没看到有人令人信服地证明它的金融效用。

turns.en: It certainly seems to have a kind of utility for, you know, sort of trading and speculation and perhaps illicit purposes, but I haven't really seen somebody identify what it's really good for in advancing certain sort of economic objectives of various kinds or just sort of commerce as it were transacting. So yeah, crypto I would lump in there too. And then, you know, I think most dubious of all are, and they're just a proposal at this point, though I did write about them, are prediction market ETFs, which would basically use what are called event contracts
turns.zh: 它似乎在交易和投机、以及也许非法用途上有一点效用，但我真的没看到有人指出它在推动各种经济目标上到底有什么用，或者说在商业、交易上有什么用。所以是的，我会把加密货币也归到那里。然后，我觉得最可疑的——尽管目前只是提议、但我确实写过——是预测市场 ETF，它们基本上会使用所谓的事件合约（event contract）——

turns.en: and allow people, I think the initial batch were tied to the outcomes of various elections, the presidential election control of either House of Congress and their binary, their zero sum, they serve no economic purpose whatsoever.
turns.zh: 让人们——我想最初一批是绑定于各种选举的结果，总统大选、对国会两院的控制——它们是二元的、零和的，没有任何经济用途。

turns.en: You know, they're really the antithesis, I think, of what people should be trying to do with their investments. And so hopefully those never see the light of day.
turns.zh: 你知道，我认为它们恰恰是人们用投资时应做的事情的反面。所以希望它们永远不见天日。

turns.en: So for people who are excited about innovations in a given sector like technology or healthcare, do you think there's any merit in setting aside a small percentage of their portfolio, maybe 5% or so as play money? Or does that just play into the type of behavioral issues that can lead to bad outcomes?
turns.zh: 那么，对于某个特定领域——比如科技或医疗保健——里那些令人兴奋的创新，你觉得拿出一小部分、比如 5% 左右作为娱乐资金（play money），可不可取？还是说那只会助长那种导致糟糕结果的行为问题？

turns.en: No, I think that's fine. And I realize for most of this conversation, I sound like the world's biggest scold, but I think it's fine to do that. But it's like you say, you want to make sure that it's on the margins.
turns.zh: 不，我觉得那没问题。我知道在这场对话里我大部分时间听起来像是世界上最爱说教的人，但我觉得那样做没关系——就像你说的，你要确保它只是处在边缘。

turns.en: You know, and one of the tricks here is just it's ensuring that it remains on the margins of your portfolio, and it doesn't come to overwhelm the other what ought to be core parts.
turns.zh: 你知道，这里的诀窍之一，就是确保它始终停留在你组合的边缘，不会压倒那些本应是核心的部分。

turns.en: The other piece of it is, you know, I think that you would want to make sure that you establish your core portfolio first, let's get that working. And then, secondarily, if you want sort of a, you know, kind of like a fun money portfolio on the side, then that's fine.
turns.zh: 另一点是，我想你会希望先确立你的核心组合，先把那套运转起来。然后其次，如果你想要一个旁边的、有点像「玩钱」的组合，那也没关系。

turns.en: But, you know, you've got your priorities in order at that point, and that ensures that you're continuing to strike a healthy balance. You recently wrote a piece where you you've been challenging several common market narratives. One was the idea that investors can meaningfully improve their outcome simply by avoiding the market's worst days.
turns.zh: 但到那时候你已经把轻重缓急排好了，这就确保你继续维持一种健康的平衡。你最近写了一篇文章，你在里面挑战了几个常见的市场叙事，其中之一就是投资者仅仅通过避开市场最糟糕的日子，就能有意义地改善自己的结果。

turns.en: What do you think these ideas, these timing myths, why do they remain so persistent? Yeah, they won't die. I think it's they're simple, you know, they're very easy to digest and into it stories and they really cut through the complexity of markets, you know, just like you think about like sort of like the miss, miss the down days, you know, narrative. And, you know, that's one that's been sort of rattling around for ages. If you just manage to miss the down days, you know, you're in great shape as an investor. And, you know, and as with a lot of these things, there's a kernel of truth to it.
turns.zh: 你觉得这些想法、这些择时神话，为什么如此难以根除？它们不会消失。我想是因为它们很简单，非常容易被消化、被讲成故事，而且它们真的穿透了市场的复杂性。想想那种「避开下跌的日子」的叙事，它已经流传了很久——你只要设法避开下跌的日子，作为投资者就形势大好。就像这些东西里很多一样，它有一小部分真相。

turns.en: And it's very sort of simple and understandable to investors of all stripes. But the problem is it doesn't tell the whole story, because the market's worst days and the market's best days cluster.
turns.zh: 它对各种类型的投资者都非常简单易懂。但问题是它没有讲出全部故事，因为市场最糟糕的日子和最精彩的日子往往扎堆出现。

turns.en: So it's virtually impossible to miss one and yet enjoy the other or vice versa. And so it's an example of how I think narratives have real staying power.
turns.zh: 所以，你几乎不可能错过其中一个却又享受到另一个，反之亦然。所以这是一个例子，说明叙事是如何有真正持久力的。

turns.en: And so I think that that's, you know, a battle that we will continue to fight to dispel some of these notions. We've done lots of research on things like tactical funds. As a group, they've been a disaster. They've done very, very poorly over long stretches of time that have included bull and bear markets alike.
turns.zh: 所以我想，那将是一场我们会继续为之奋战的战斗，去破除这些观念。我们对战术型基金（tactical fund）之类做了很多研究，作为一个整体，它们是一场灾难，在包含牛市和熊市的漫长时段里表现非常非常差。

turns.en: And so it, you know, it just really, I think, should put to rest this notion that people can swallow them around the market in the way some would suggest it's not the case the data doesn't support that.
turns.zh: 所以，我想它确实应该让人放下那种人们可以像某些人所说的那样在市场周围腾挪的观点——情况并非如此，数据并不支持这一点。

turns.en: So when it comes to portfolio construction, if you were kind of starting out in building a portfolio from scratch, what are the asset classes that you would want to either include or exclude?
turns.zh: 那么，谈到组合构建，如果你要从零开始搭建一个组合，你会想纳入或排除哪些资产类别？

turns.en: And do you think investors should have exposure to things like REITs, crypto, gold commodities, et cetera? So I think if you invest in a target date fund, not that people have to do that, but they can sort of use that as maybe sort of the prototype for, you know, sort of where to try to get exposure, achieve diversification.
turns.zh: 你觉得投资者应该有一些像 REITs、加密货币、黄金、大宗商品之类的敞口吗？所以我想，如果你投资一只目标日期基金——并不是说人们非得这么做，但他们可以把它当作一个获取敞口、实现分散化的原型——

turns.en: You know, that's a pretty good starting point. And that's going to span stocks and bonds, domestic and foreign developed and emerging markets.
turns.zh: 那是个不错的起点，它会横跨股票和债券、国内和海外、发达市场和新兴市场。

turns.en: I think some of the popular target date funds, they do also include exposure to things like REITs. And that's fine. You know, they are correlated with equities.
turns.zh: 我想一些流行的目标日期基金确实也包含了像 REITs（房地产投资信托）之类的敞口，那没关系——它们与股票是相关的。

turns.en: You know, so they're not like this super, super potent diversifier. And I think you've done quite a bit of work on that, looking at that in particular.
turns.zh: 所以它们不是那种超级有效的分散化工具。而且我想你在这方面、尤其这一点上做过不少研究。

turns.en: You know, it's fine that they're in there. They do exclude things. So many of them exclude high yield bonds. Again, I think that that is forgivable, given high yield bonds tend to be quite correlated with equities.
turns.zh: 它们在那里没关系。它们确实排除了一些东西——很多目标日期基金排除高收益债（high yield bond）。我又觉得，鉴于高收益债往往与股票高度相关，这是可以原谅的。

turns.en: And, you know, in many cases, we're looking for that bond portion to provide ballast when equities get themselves into trouble. The other things that you mentioned, Crypto Gold Commodities, to me, those seem extraneous. They're not must haves. You know, the one other that I would throw in there that I think in a number of leading target date funds, it's not present.
turns.zh: 在很多情况下，我们希望债券那部分在股票出麻烦时起到压舱石（ballast）的作用。你提到的其他东西——加密货币、黄金、大宗商品——在我看来是多余的，它们不是必备项。我会加进去、而我认为在许多领先的目标日期基金里并不存在的另一样东西——

turns.en: It would be tips. So having some exposure to tips, I think is advisable. It's a good compliment to your core bond allocation, you know, and so throwing in an allocation to tips as well.
turns.zh: 会是 TIPS（通胀保值国债）。所以有一些 TIPS 敞口我觉得是可取的，它对你核心的债券配置是很好的补充，所以再加上一份 TIPS 的配置。

turns.en: You know, I think that gets you largely to where you need to be. Which current market narrative do you think has the shortest shelf life? Yeah, I'm terrible with this sort of thing. I don't know about shortest shelf life, but I wrote a piece not too long ago, and it couldn't have been more facile.
turns.zh: 我想这基本就把你带到了需要去的地方。你认为哪个当前市场叙事的保质期最短？你知道，我不擅长这类东西，我不知道哪个保质期最短，但我不久前写了一篇文章，它再简单不过了。

turns.en: But it was one in which I cast out in the sustainability of the tech sector's returns. You know, as we know, performance has been fabulous for a very long time in that sector.
turns.zh: 但在那篇文章里，我对科技板块回报的可持续性提出了质疑。我们都知道，那个板块的业绩长期以来一直非常出色。

turns.en: And, you know, based on the research that I did, I don't think it portends very well for the future. I think I found that any time a sector had a rolling 10-year return of 20% or more per year, it lost money over the next decade, every time.
turns.zh: 根据我做的研究，我觉得它对前景未必乐观。我发现，只要某个板块有过 20% 或以上的滚动 10 年年化回报，接下来十年它都会亏钱——每一次都如此。

turns.en: And so, you know, I think it's become writ in some circles that tech will continue to leave the market as it has. But, you know, my analysis suggests you should be so sure.
turns.zh: 所以，我想在某些圈子里已经是不言自明，科技会继续像过去那样领跑市场，但我的分析告诉你——别那么笃定。

turns.en: So that's probably an example of, you know, what has become sort of a dominant narrative, you know, that I think people might want a question.
turns.zh: 所以，那大概就是一个已经成主流叙事的例子，我觉得人们或许想要对此提出质疑。

turns.en: So if people are wary of tech stocks, especially those that have really high valuations, is there an area that you would kind of tilt toward to offset some of that risk?
turns.zh: 那么，如果人们警惕科技股，尤其是那些估值非常高的科技股，你会不会倾向于往某个领域倾斜，来抵消一些那种风险？

turns.en: Not really. This is me at my most defeatist, but I think this is the paradox. We've gone through periods like this before where an area gets really, really hot.
turns.zh: 不太会。这是我最为悲观的时候，但我觉得这就是那个悖论。我们以前也经历过类似这样的阶段，某个领域会变得非常非常炙热。

turns.en: And, you know, while tech valuations are not blaring alarm at this point, given sort of the earnings acceleration that we've seen across certain subsectors within tech, you know, I think after you've gone to run the likes tech has, I think there's some reason to question the sustainability of that.
turns.zh: 虽然眼下科技估值还算不上在拉响警报，考虑到我们在科技内部某些子板块看到的盈利加速，但我觉得，在科技走出像它那样的长牛之后，有理由去质疑这种势头能持续多久。

turns.en: But what you do tend to find in indexes is you'll have another sector area that takes the baton and leads the market higher in its next phase offsetting some of the weakness that you're seeing in a sector that had formerly led. And so, you know, that's what gives me some reassurance that this is the sort of thing that, you know, investors diversified investors index investors in which tech is a big weight.
turns.zh: 但在指数里你往往会发现，会有另一个板块接过接力棒，在市场的下一个阶段带领大盘走高，从而抵消了你此前领跑的那个板块所显现的一些疲弱。所以，这让我多少有些宽慰——对于那些分散化投资者、指数投资者来说（而科技在其中占很大权重）——这类事情……

turns.en: We'll get through this. They'll be able to withstand it. But I think it's going to be tougher sledding for tech, even based on this very, very facile analysis that I did.
turns.zh: ……会熬过去的，他们能够承受得住。但我想，科技接下来的路会更难走，哪怕只是基于我做的这个非常非常简单的分析。

turns.en: So, Jeff, you are not a stranger to this podcast. You helped launch it with me back in 2019. As you reflect on the many episodes that you worked on with me, what were a couple of your favorites?
turns.zh: 所以，Jeff，你对这档播客并不陌生。你 2019 年和我一起创办了它。回顾你和我一起做的那么多期节目，你的最爱有哪几期？

turns.en: You referenced the Bess and Binder one, which was super good. But were there any others that stand out in your mind? Yeah, the episode with longevity researcher Laura Carstensen, that one is memorable to me. You know, meaning and purpose are so intrinsic to who we are. And I thought she did a great job of explaining why that's especially true in retirement.
turns.zh: 你提到了 Bessembinder 那期，非常好。但还有别的让你印象深刻的吗？是的，和长寿研究者 Laura Carstensen 的那期让我记忆犹新。意义和目标对我们是谁至关重要，我觉得她把这一点为何在退休阶段尤其如此，解释得非常好。

turns.en: That was a great episode. I also loved our sort of born in an investing vein. I loved our conversations with with David Drew. He's a great investor, and he doesn't rest on his laurels. Another David David hero at Oakmark.
turns.zh: 那是很棒的一期。我也很喜欢我们那些偏投资风格的对话——我很喜欢我们和 David Dreer 的对话，他是很棒的投资者，而且不故步自封。还有另一位 David，David Herro，在 Oakmark。

turns.en: Yeah, I thought he radiated the same quality. He just he loves the game. And it just it really came across in our conversation with him. And then, you know, lastly, I know I'm throwing out a few here.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得他身上散发着同样的品质——他就是热爱这份事业，这一点在我们和他的对话里真的表现得很明显。然后，我知道我这儿列举了好几个。

turns.en: But the last one I would mention was prime cap. You know, that was kind of a, in a way, a career highlight for me. I had had the opportunity to cover them in a former life.
turns.zh: 但我最后要提的是 Primecap。你知道，那在某种程度上是我职业生涯的一个高光。我在早年的工作里曾有机会覆盖过他们。

turns.en: You know, but this was a chance for the world to hear from them. They're pretty selective. I think, as you know, about media appearances, public appearances.
turns.zh: 但这次是让全世界有机会听到他们的声音。他们对媒体和公开露面一直很挑剔，我想你也知道。

turns.en: And so just really grateful to have had the chance for us to speak to Joel Freed and Al Mordechie as we did. You know, it was it was really cool to do that.
turns.zh: 所以，我们有机会和 Joel Freed 与 Al Maromnejad 对话，我真的很感激，那真的非常棒。

turns.en: You've also been a key contributor to our state of retirement income report in previous years. And I'm curious if any of that research has changed your thinking about any aspects of retirement planning or personal finance?
turns.zh: 过去几年，你也一直是我们 State of Retirement Income 报告的关键贡献者。我很好奇，那些研究有没有改变你对退休规划或个人理财某些方面的看法？

turns.en: Yeah, the irony is, I think it's helped me appreciate how there's a lot more to it than the number. You too. And also, John Reckentahler, when he was one of our collaborators in the study a few years ago.
turns.zh: 是的，有意思的是，我觉得它让我更加体会到，其中的内涵远不止那个数字本身。你也一样，还有 John Wregen，当他几年前是我们这项研究的合作者之一时。

turns.en: You know, I think you have just done an awesome job of helping retirees think about the various tradeoffs associated with the different approaches. And you know, and you've continued to add these different sort of approaches.
turns.zh: 我觉得你把帮助退休者思考不同方法所涉及的种种取舍，做得太出色了，而且你一直在加入这些不同的方法。

turns.en: And I think it's it's really helped people to understand the levers that they can pull and, you know, sort of the different sort of priorities that they might have to balance off when it comes to spending and maybe how efficient it is or, you know, how strong their bequest motive is and, you know, what might be the right approach to fit that. So it's really opened my eyes to those those different dimensions and the different choices that one can make. So it's really a tribute to the work that you've done.
turns.zh: 我觉得它真的帮助人们理解了他们能拉动哪些杠杆，以及在支出上可能要去平衡的种种不同优先级、效率有多高、他们的遗赠动机（bequest motive）有多强，以及什么方法可能最适合它。所以它真的让我开阔了眼界，看到了这些不同维度以及一个人可以做出的不同选择，所以这真的是对你所做工作的一种致敬。

turns.en: I always like to ask about sources of inspiration, podcasts, blogs, and so on. Can you talk about some of your favorites? I know you're an avid reader and consumer of podcasts as well.
turns.zh: 我总是喜欢问关于灵感来源的问题，播客、博客等等。你能谈谈你的一些最爱吗？我知道你也是一位热心的读者和播客消费者。

turns.en: I would say at the risk of being a little corny, I would say in addition to the two of you and folks like John Wreckentahler, Russ Kinnell, who I think we might have mentioned earlier, others here at Morningstar who are such gifted writers and also very generous in sharing their wisdom with others and those, you know, are facing various personal finance or portfolio construction questions. You know, I would say there's a few luminaries, you know, who I've gone back to, one, a very familiar name to all of us that would be Bogle and Common Sense on Mutual Funds I think is a great book.
turns.zh: 冒着有点老套的风险，我想说，除了你们两位，还有像 John Wregen、Russ Kinnell——我想我们之前可能提到过——这样在 Morningstar 的同事们，他们是有天赋的写作者，也毫不吝啬地把自己的智慧分享给正在面对各种个人理财或组合构建问题的人。要说几位我反复回去读的大师，一个我们都再熟悉不过的名字就是 Bogle，《The Commonsense Book of Investing》我认为是一本很棒的书。

turns.en: It's timeless, diversify, minimize costs, avoid over-transacting. It's kind of all you need in terms of, you know, investing parables that I think will become even more relevant as time wears on when genius failed by Roger Lowenstein.
turns.zh: 它历久弥新：分散化、把成本降到最小、避免过度交易。就投资的寓言而言，这几乎就是你所需的一切，我想随着时间推移它会变得越来越贴切。Roger Lowenstein 的《When Genius Failed》。

turns.en: It's a fantastic, fantastic story and, you know, Roger's very learned and I think he does a good job not just of constructing the narrative but also helping people to understand, you know, what are the enduring lessons of the LTCM affair.
turns.zh: 那是一个非常精彩的故事，Roger 学识渊博，我觉得他不仅把叙事构建得很好，也帮助人们理解了 LTCM 事件那些长存的教训。

turns.en: And then lastly, anything by Jason Swig. Jason spent on the podcast several times and deservedly so. Any of his books are worth returning to. Those three are about as good as it gets.
turns.zh: 最后一点，Jason Zweig 的任何作品。Jason 上过这档播客好几次，实至名归。他的任何一本书都值得反复去读。这三本差不多就是最好的了。

turns.en: Well, thanks so much, Jeff, for taking the time to talk with us today. It's great to catch up with you on some of your research and your take on the overall market.
turns.zh: Jeff，非常感谢你今天抽出时间和我们聊天。能和你聊聊你的一些研究，以及你对整体市场的看法，真是太好了。

turns.en: Well, thank you so much. It's been a real pleasure. You're wonderful, Jeff. Thank you. Thank you for joining us on the Long View. If you could, please take a moment to subscribe to and rate the podcast on Apple, Spotify or wherever you get your podcasts.
turns.zh: 非常感谢，这是一次真正的愉快。你太棒了，Jeff，谢谢你。谢谢你做客《The Long View》。如果可以的话，请在 Apple、Spotify 或你收听播客的任何平台花点时间订阅并给这档节目评分。

turns.en: You can follow me on social media at Amy Arnot on LinkedIn and at Christine Benz on LinkedIn or at Christine Underscore Benz on X. George Castady is our engineer for the podcast. Jessica Bebel produces the show notes each week and Jennifer Garrett copy edits our transcripts.
turns.zh: 你可以在 LinkedIn 上关注我和 Amy Arnott，在 LinkedIn 上关注 Christine Benz，或在 X 上关注 Christine_Underscore_Benz。George Kabadze 是我们这档播客的工程师，Jessica Bebel 每周制作节目注记，Jennifer Garrett 负责给我们逐字稿做文字校对。

turns.en: Finally, we'd love to get your feedback. If you have a comment or a guest idea, please email us at thelongviewatmorningstar.com. Until next time, thanks for joining us.
turns.zh: 最后，我们很想听听你的反馈。如果你有意见或嘉宾建议，请发邮件到 thelongview@morningstar.com。下次见之前，感谢你的收听。
